additional_notes: Used with feminine singular or plural nouns to mean 'have no' or 'don't have any'. With a neuter singular object, use haben kein.
Einen is masculine accusative singular. Hat can express possession or serve as the auxiliary in the perfect tense.
Means 'she has', or 'it has' when referring to a feminine noun. Hat can also form the perfect tense. Sentence-initial Sie hat still means 'she/it has'; formal 'you have' is Sie haben.
Informal singular imperative: 'tell her'. Sag addresses one person of any gender; ihr refers to the female recipient.
Means 'is it?' in questions or 'it is' after a fronted element. In constructions such as etwas gewohnt sein, es can instead be an object referring to what someone is used to.
